title: Who Are You, Really?
description: Checking whether five Canadian B2B brands were described consistently across search and AI.

sections.heading: Identity facts can disagree
sections.body: The study found conflicting founding years for three of five brands. Even familiar businesses can have multiple versions of their history circulating across search and AI surfaces.

sections.heading: Visibility does not guarantee consistency
sections.body: For two brands, Google’s knowledge panel and AI Mode disagreed on a checked fact. A visible panel should not be treated as proof that every surface shares the same entity information.

sections.heading: Start with a factual reference
sections.body: A useful next step is a dated, sourced record of founding history, founders, headquarters and leadership. It makes discrepancies easier to investigate without assuming the AI answer is the authority.

methodology: A comparison of Shopify, Hootsuite, Clio, Unbounce and Jane App on 22 October 2026. Four identity facts were checked across Google knowledge panels, ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and public web sources.
limitations: Facts and interfaces can change. These are dated observations, not a statement about current leadership or current search results. Differences may reflect ambiguity in how a founding date or location is defined.
